topic: Earth's Tilt and Its Effect on Seasons
key_concepts: Earth rotates on its axis, causing the diurnal cycle of lightness and darkness
Earth's rotation period is approximately 24 hours or 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds
Earth revolves around the Sun in approximately 365.25 days
Earth's axial tilt is approximately 23.5 degrees
The equator receives the greatest intensity of the Sun's rays
Places farther from the equator receive less heat because sunlight strikes at a lower angl
The coldest regions on Earth are typically near the poles due to low-angle sunlight
High-temperature regions are typically near the equator because sunlight is direct or near
Earth's tilt causes seasons as Earth orbits the Sun
March and September are equinoxes with nearly equal daylight and night
June and December are solstices with unequal daylight and night
The Sun's path and noon angle in the sky change with the seasons
